etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English fers, fiers, borrowed from Old French fers (“wild", "ferocious”), nominative of fer, from Latin ferus (“wild", "untamed”).

definitions.definition: Exceedingly violent, severe, ferocious, cruel or savage.

quote.text: Their fights with other members of their own kind were always preceded by loud and fierce waulings or savage snarling and snapping of teeth  […]

quote.citation: 2012, Michael Bryant, 28 Seconds: A True Story of Addiction, Tragedy, and Hope, Viking:
quote.text: One constituent spent an hour educating me on the history of pit bulls: the Molossians, the Mastiffs; the Greeks, Romans, Brits, Tibetans, and Germans; the crossbreeds. A common theme ran throughout their history: they were the fiercest of fighters, and eventually bred to fight—in wars during antiquity, in dog fights for centuries. Regardless, they were again and again attacking other dogs and people.

quote.citation: 1902, John Buchan, The Outgoing of the Tide:
quote.text: Yet his passion for her had grown fiercer than ever, and he swore to himself that he would win her back from her phantasies. She, one may believe, was ready enough to listen.

definitions.definition: (US, LGBTQ slang, fashion) Of exceptional quality, exhibiting boldness or chutzpah.
